paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: only the LORD tells the future and then makes it happen. In this courtroom, the LORD asks the idols to "Tell us the things that are to come" (Isaiah 41:23), and they have nothing to say (Isaiah 41:28). The LORD, meanwhile, says He was the first to tell Zion (Isaiah 41:27). Whoever can name the ending before it happens is the One worth listening to.

Now, why does that matter to you? Because everybody follows something. Money, a schedule, a feed full of voices all telling you what's next. The LORD's verdict on the idols is that "their images are as empty as the wind" (Isaiah 41:29), and I think that's a kind word for anybody tempted to lean on them. A lot of things sound confident, friend, but confident and right are not the same thing.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. The LORD isn't hiding. He says what He will do, and then He does it, and you can check His work. I spent years in a drawer, waiting on a promise I couldn't see, and I would have given anything for a voice that could be trusted like that. You have one. Build your days on Him, and you won't be building on wind.
